perspective:
Keith has access to the following information:

- He is Keith Ndiaye, a construction worker. Elizabeth Sun is his colleague, the receptionist at the same construction company; they have a friendly, professional relationship and interact when he visits the office for paperwork or project updates.
- Recently, Keith observed Elizabeth being unusually curt or short with him over several days. He wondered if he had unknowingly upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and that she was sorry if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic toward her. He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to be someone she could talk to, and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept, thank him, and say that sounded good.
- During the coffee break, Keith heard Elizabeth share more about her personal stresses, which seemed severe to him. He suggested she consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can help. He heard her say she had thought about it, was unsure, and was hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, Keith observed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her. He heard her say he hadn’t overstepped, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. He believes she values his support and feels more comfortable around him now. He told her he was glad they talked and that he is always available to chat or take breaks. He heard her thank him, say it meant a lot, and say she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith’s own intention is to maintain this supportive relationship with Elizabeth.
